rules.subject: public_circulation
rules.rationale: Public, staff and service flows are kept apart: visitors do not walk the routes that carry supplies, waste and the dead, and service traffic does not cross the public lobby.
exceptions: Shared lifts used out of hours under control

rules.subject: emergency_department
rules.rationale: Emergency patients, on foot and by ambulance, arrive at an entrance of their own, separate from the main lobby, so urgent cases do not queue with outpatients.
exceptions: Very small hospitals with a single entrance and a triage desk

rules.subject: ambulance_bay
rules.rationale: The sickest patients take the shortest path from the ambulance to resuscitation, without crossing the waiting area.

rules.subject: patient_room
rules.rationale: Patient privacy: inpatient rooms and wards are reached through a controlled ward door, never straight from the public lobby or its corridors.
exceptions: Visiting hours with an open ward door

rules.subject: nurse_station
rules.rationale: A ward's nurse station has sightlines to the patient rooms it serves, so nurses can see and reach a patient quickly.
exceptions: Decentralised nursing with alcoves between rooms

rules.subject: clean_utility
rules.rationale: Clean supplies and dirty (soiled) material are held in separate rooms on separate routes, so they do not cross-contaminate. How strictly the routes must differ is contested, see the conflict ledger.
exceptions: Older hospitals with a single OR corridor and strict procedure

rules.subject: operating_theatre
rules.rationale: Operating rooms sit in a restricted zone entered through a scrub area or sterile corridor, so patients and staff change status before they are inside it.
exceptions: Minor procedure rooms outside the surgical suite

rules.subject: intensive_care
rules.rationale: Patients move from surgery to intensive care in minutes, so the unit is close to the operating rooms, and ideally to the emergency department too.
exceptions: Hospitals that reach it by a dedicated lift

rules.subject: imaging
rules.rationale: The emergency department is a heavy user of X-ray and CT, so imaging close to it shortens urgent transport.
exceptions: A central imaging department placed on main circulation to serve every unit

rules.subject: isolation_room
rules.rationale: An isolation room is entered through an anteroom, so air and people are not exchanged directly with the general ward.

rules.subject: pharmacy
rules.rationale: The central pharmacy holds controlled drugs, so it is reached through staff-only doors; an outpatient window may face the public side.
exceptions: An outpatient dispensing window on the public side

rules.subject: mortuary
rules.rationale: The mortuary is reached by a discreet service route and is not entered from public circulation.

rules.subject: loading_dock
rules.rationale: Deliveries come in at a dock that opens onto the service corridor, the route to stores, pharmacy and sterile processing.

rules.subject: outpatient_waiting
rules.rationale: Outpatients are mostly able to walk, so their waiting area opens off public circulation near the lobby, which keeps clinic traffic out of the wards and off the service routes.
exceptions: Day wards for dialysis or oncology inside an inpatient unit
A separate outpatient building with its own entrance

rules.subject: exam_room
rules.condition: the hospital's outpatient or clinic wing
rules.rationale: Outpatient exam rooms open off a clinical corridor, not off each other and not off the waiting area. Whether they also have a second staff door is contested, see the conflict ledger.
exceptions: Dual-door rooms with a separate staff door

rules.subject: exam_room
rules.rationale: Patient privacy: exam and consult room doors do not open onto the waiting area, so a patient being examined cannot be seen or heard from the seats. A drawing still needs a person's review for door swing and sightlines.
exceptions: Fast-track or minor-injury bays that open from a shared treatment hall

rules.subject: nurse_alcove
rules.rationale: In the outpatient wing the nurse and support alcove, for charting, medication preparation and clean supply, sits next to the cluster of exam rooms it serves.
exceptions: Wall cabinets or carts in each exam room replace a clean room

conflicts.topic: How strictly clean and dirty routes must differ

positions.position: The routes must be completely separate throughout the hospital, with no exception (confidence 0.95).
Separate rooms and routes, but a one-way pass-through room may link the two by design.
Separate corridors are the norm around operating rooms, though older hospitals manage with one corridor and strict procedure.

conflicts.resolution: The rule asks only that the two utility rooms be separate; that every route be separate is not adopted, since two of the three allow exceptions.

conflicts.topic: One corridor or two for exam rooms

positions.position: Exam rooms are reached only through the clinical corridor.
A second door onto a staff corridor lets clinicians move without crossing the patient corridor; the evidence is mixed (confidence 0.5).
One clinical corridor, with dual-door rooms as an exception.

conflicts.resolution: The rule requires the clinical corridor door and says nothing of a second one.
